steps.name: connect-hook benchmark measures the gateway hook against no hook
steps.description: The cgroup-connect-hook family and the pig-connect-cost spike use the arms no-hook (reference, the gateway program's cgroup link detached) and gateway-hook, because the boot attaches only the gateway connect program. The spike is re-run first on the same arms; its values become the family's references; E-1 is re-run.
steps.implementation_notes: Exact contract in feature-delta 'Connect-hook family' (arms, metrics, identification of the gateway program, references) and K2 (a) to (d). Commit cfcc67612 deleted the service cgroup_connect4 program, so smoke_connect_hook_cost fails at HEAD until this step. Identification: take the programs that appeared after the pre-load program set, keep those named cgroup_connect4 (the kernel truncation of cgroup_connect4_gateway), require exactly one, and confirm it references the map named GATEWAY_CONNECT; zero, several or an unconfirmed one fails the replicate naming what was found. gateway-hook records hook_ns_per_connect from that program's run_time_ns and run_count deltas; no-hook records record_absent('hook_ns_per_connect', 'no connect program is attached on this arm'), never zero. Under smoke both arms record it absent. The spike crate declares the same arms and no reference. Order: (1) family and spike change, smoke passes in cgroup-default; (2) run the spike on Metal, pull, validate, commit under a new run id; (3) put its gateway-hook median hook time and its wall-time delta in the family's two references with the pinned labels and the spike report as source; (4) run E-1 on Metal, pull, validate, commit under a new run id. The records taken against the two-program dataplane (benchmarks/results/cgroup-connect-hook/ E-1 to E-3 and spike-scratch/pig-connect-cost/results/cgroup-connect-hook/afda96dd5b779f7516937a4f) are history: leave them in place, do not re-render them. K2 (b) checks that the record and report carry the wall_ns_per_connect delta, its bootstrap interval, the A/A interval and the verdict; either verdict is accepted and reported as observed, never retried or chosen. Catalogue row wording: arms no-hook (reference, gateway link detached, nothing attached on the cgroup) and gateway-hook; workload: the gateway connect program the dataplane boot attaches, 500 warm-up then 5,000 timed loopback connect-and-close, 30 replicates per arm; clock boundary: hook_ns_per_connect is the gateway program's kernel run_time_ns over run_count on gateway-hook only (absent on no-hook), wall_ns_per_connect is host CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW stamps around the timed loop divided by 5,000 and its delta contains the cgroup-BPF dispatch cost. Prerequisites: bpf-build, kmod-build, guest-kit-prepare, exclusive kmod-load.
criteria: The family declares arms no-hook (reference) and gateway-hook; hook_ns_per_connect is recorded on gateway-hook and absent with the pinned reason on no-hook; the gateway program is identified as pinned; generated smoke_connect_hook_cost passes in cgroup-default

The pig-connect-cost spike declares the same arms with no reference and is re-run with cargo xtask metal run --benchmark cgroup-connect-hook --spike pig-connect-cost; record and report are pulled, bench-report validate exits 0, and they are committed under spike-scratch/pig-connect-cost/results/cgroup-connect-hook/<new-run-id>/ with the earlier run left in place

The family's two references hold the re-run spike's gateway-hook hook-time median and wall-time delta, with the labels spike evidence, different run, gateway-hook median and spike evidence, different run, gateway-hook minus no-hook delta, and the spike report as source

steps.name: a partly failed series keeps its measured values
steps.description: A series metric entry of an ok replicate holds its measured values and its failures together, so a stage that fails for one workload at concurrency 4 no longer discards the values the other workloads measured.
steps.implementation_notes: Exact contract in feature-delta DDD-6 'Partly measured series' and the Replicate method comments; no new method, no new record field, schema stays 1. Replicate: record_series and record_failure on one series metric are accepted in either order and the metric holds both; record_failure after a scalar record, record_absent on a metric holding values or failures, and record_series or record_failure on an absent metric stay a ReplicateFailure. The recording is written as the existing four-field entry with values or histogram (a series of more than 1,000 values is a histogram, failures alongside) and failures together. Validator: an ok replicate's scalar entry holds exactly one of a value, failures or absent; a series entry holds measured, failures, both, or absent alone; the two messages are pinned in DDD-6. Statistics are unchanged in form: values feed the distribution, the failures column still counts replicates, ## Failures lists one line per reason; confirm report.rs needs no change. The vm-lifecycle record_cycles (stage metrics) records every workload's value with record_series and every failure with record_failure, and records absent only when no workload reached the stage; guest_shutdown_handling_ns keeps its form. Retained records must still validate: run bench-report validate over every record under benchmarks/results and spike-scratch/pig-connect-cost/results. benchmarks/methodology.md failure accounting gains one sentence stating that a partly measured series keeps both. Acceptance scenario bodies (validate accepts and refuses the entry shapes, the report counts a partly measured series, the retained records validate) are authored by the acceptance designer in a DISTILL addendum before this step; the crafter does not write them. No Metal re-run of vm-lifecycle is required by this step.
criteria: bench-report validate accepts a series entry holding values (or a histogram) together with failures in an ok replicate, and refuses a scalar entry combining a value with failures, any entry combining absent with values or failures, and an entry holding nothing, with the pinned messages naming the metric

Replicate record_series and record_failure on one series metric accept either order and the written entry holds both; the pinned refusals for scalar, absent and undeclared metrics hold; the replicate stays ok
The report counts a partly measured entry in replicates and in failures, pools its values into the percentiles, feeds its replicate median into the delta, and lists each failure reason under Failures
The vm-lifecycle family records each workload's value or failure per stage without discarding either, and a stage metric is absent only when no workload reached it
Every retained record under benchmarks/results and spike-scratch/pig-connect-cost/results still validates with bench-report validate, and the methodology failure accounting states the rule
